s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Provision):
List-I | List-II
a. 15(4) | i. Autonomous State within Assam (22nd Amendment, 1969)
b. 244(2) | ii. Special provisions for SEBCs, SCs, STs – added by the 1st Amendment, 1951
c. 244A | iii. Sixth Schedule – Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
d. 339 | iv. Union control of Scheduled Areas and ST welfare
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 15(4) – first reservation clause (1st Amendment 1951); 244(2) – Sixth Schedule tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; 244A – Autonomous State within Assam (22nd Amendment 1969); 339 – Union control of Scheduled Areas.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 94th Amendment (2006) replaced Bihar with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand in the proviso to Article 164(1).
2. Scheduled Areas are declared under Article 339.
3. The special provisions for SCs, STs, BCs and Anglo-Indians (Articles 330-342A) are in Part XVI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Scheduled Areas are declared under paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule; Art. 339 is Union control of their administration.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Scheduled Castes are defined in Article 366(25) and Scheduled Tribes in Article 366(24).
2. Articles 341, 342 and 342A deal with the lists of SCs, STs and SEBCs respectively.
3. Article 334 sets the time limit on reservation of seats for SCs and STs, now up to 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the clauses are the other way round – 366(24) defines SCs and 366(25) defines STs.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Grants-in-aid under Article 275(1) are regarded as an economic safeguard for Scheduled Tribes.
Reason (R): Article 275(1) provides grants-in-aid from the Centre for the welfare of STs and for Scheduled Areas.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: because 275(1) channels Central grants for ST welfare and Scheduled Areas, it is grouped as the economic safeguard for STs.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Article 325 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes.
Reason (R): Article 325 bars the exclusion of any person from the electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: Art. 325 gives no reservation (seats are reserved under 330 and 332). R is true: it only guarantees a single general electoral roll without caste exclusion.

s:
Consider the following statements about reserved seats for SCs and STs in legislatures:
1. They are filled through separate electorates of SC/ST voters.
2. Article 334 originally fixed the reservation for 10 years.
3. The 104th Amendment (2019) extended it to 2030 and ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: there is no separate electorate – all voters of the constituency elect the SC/ST member.

s:
Match List-I (Constitutional Amendment) with List-II (Effect):
List-I | List-II
a. 8th (1959) | i. Refixed seats on the 1991 Census
b. 51st (1984) | ii. Extended SC/ST seat reservation to 2020
c. 84th | iii. ST Lok Sabha seats for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal and Mizoram
d. 95th (2009) | iv. Extended SC/ST seat reservation to 1970
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 8th – to 1970; 51st – ST seats in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal, Mizoram; 84th – seats refixed on the 1991 Census (87th on 2001); 95th – to 2020 (now 2030 by the 104th).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the 2008 delimitation, 79 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for SCs and 41 for STs.
2. Andhra Pradesh has 4 SC and 1 ST (Araku) seats among its 25 Lok Sabha seats.
3. Andhra Pradesh has 29 SC and 7 ST seats in its 175-member Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: 79 SC / 41 ST was the 1971-Census position; after the 2008 delimitation it is 84 SC / 47 ST.

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 17:
1. It is in the Right to Equality group, and Ambedkar ensured that untouchability became a punishable offence.
2. The expression 'untouchability' is defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
3. Under Article 35(a)(ii), only Parliament can prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution or in any Act; the Mysore HC read it as the practice as historically developed.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Article 17 can be enforced against private persons.
Reason (R): In PUDR v Union of India (1982), the Supreme Court held that Article 17 binds private persons too.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: Art. 17 operates horizontally, as held in PUDR (1982).

s:
Consider the following statements about the term 'Scheduled Castes':
1. It was first used by the Simon Commission.
2. The first list under the Government of India Act, 1935 was issued in 1936.
3. The first post-1950 list was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the first post-1950 list was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was the first law enforcing Article 23.
2. Johan Galtung's 'structural violence' means harm built into social structures.
3. In the Sabarimala reference, Justice B.V. Nagarathna said Article 17 cannot apply 'for three days a month'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the 1955 Act was the first law enforcing Article 17; Art. 23 is about forced labour.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013:
1. It came into force on 6 December 2013 and bans insanitary latrines.
2. Hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks is permitted when done through private contractors.
3. Offences under it are cognizable and non-bailable.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: hazardous sewer/septic cleaning is banned for anyone, including private contractors.

s:
Consider the following statements about penalties under the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013:
1. Its implementation is monitored by the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
2. A first breach is punishable with up to 1 year and/or ₹50,000.
3. A first breach involving hazardous sewer cleaning is punishable with up to 2 years and/or ₹2 lakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK) monitors the Act.

s:
Match List-I (Law / scheme) with List-II (Key point):
List-I | List-II
a. 1993 Act | i. Self-employment scheme with NSKFDC (1997) as nodal agency
b. Rashtriya Garima Abhiyan (2001) | ii. National Campaign for Dignity to eradicate manual scavenging
c. SRMS (2007) | iii. Prohibited employment of manual scavengers and construction of dry latrines
d. NAMASTE (2023) | iv. MoSJE + MoHUA scheme for zero sanitation fatalities
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 1993 Act – Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition); Rashtriya Garima Abhiyan – campaign for dignity; SRMS – self-employment scheme, NSKFDC nodal, now subsumed in NAMASTE; NAMASTE – MoSJE with MoHUA, zero sanitation fatalities.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In Safai Karamchari Andolan v UOI (2014), the Supreme Court fixed ₹10 lakh compensation for each sewer death since 1993.
2. Bandicoot, the manhole-cleaning robot, was developed by ISRO.
3. In Balram Singh (2023) the compensation was raised to ₹30 lakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Bandicoot was developed by the Kerala start-up Genrobotics; ISRO's Vyommitra is a humanoid.

s:
Match List-I (Body / scheme) with List-II (Focus):
List-I | List-II
a. NSFDC | i. Movement co-founded by Bezwada Wilson
b. NSKFDC | ii. Sanitation workers
c. PM-DAKSH | iii. Scheduled Castes below the poverty line
d. Safai Karmachari Andolan | iv. Skill development
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: NSFDC – BPL SCs; NSKFDC – sanitation workers; PM-DAKSH – skills; Safai Karmachari Andolan – co-founded by Bezwada Wilson (Magsaysay 2016).

s:
Consider the following statements about the list of Scheduled Castes:
1. Under Article 341, the President specifies the SCs of a State after consulting its Governor.
2. Castes can be added to the list by a later Presidential notification.
3. States have no power over the list – the Supreme Court in 2024 quashed Bihar's 2015 notification moving Tanti-Tantwa to the SC list.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: under Art. 341(2) inclusion or exclusion is only by Parliament by law, not by a later notification.

s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011:
1. Scheduled Castes formed 16.6% of India's population.
2. Uttar Pradesh has the highest share of SCs in its population.
3. SCs formed 17.08% of Andhra Pradesh's population, with an SC literacy rate of 64.47%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Punjab has the highest SC share; Uttar Pradesh has the largest SC population in number.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Madiga Dandora movement:
1. It was launched in 1994 by Manda Krishna Madiga at Eedumudi in Prakasam district.
2. It alleged that the Madigas dominated the 15% SC quota.
3. The Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission (1996) placed the Malas in Category C.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the movement alleged Mala dominance of the quota and demanded A-B-C-D sub-classification.

s:
Match List-I (Commission) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08) | i. Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes
b. K.G. Balakrishnan Commission (2022) | ii. Amend Article 341 to let States sub-categorise SCs
c. Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission (2017) | iii. SC status for Dalit converts
d. Rajiv Gauba panel (2024) | iv. Most backward SC sub-castes
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Usha Mehra – amend Art. 341 for sub-categorisation; K.G. Balakrishnan – SC status for Dalit converts; Idate – DNTs/NTs/SNTs (led to SEED); Rajiv Gauba – most backward SC sub-castes.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh was the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by statute.
Reason (R): The AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000 was upheld by the Supreme Court in E.V. Chinnaiah.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true (AP Act 2000). R is false: Chinnaiah (2004) struck the Act down, holding SCs a single class; that view was overruled only in Davinder Singh (2024).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The original Article 338 provided for a Special Officer (Commissioner for SCs and STs).
2. The joint National Commission for SCs and STs became a constitutional body in 1978.
3. The 89th Amendment (2003) split it; the NCST under Article 338A came into being on 19 February 2004.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 1978 Commission was non-statutory; the joint Commission became constitutional in 1990.

s:
Consider the following statements about the NCSC and NCST:
1. Each has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members.
2. The NCST Chairperson holds Cabinet rank.
3. They present their reports directly to Parliament.
4. Under Article 338(9), the Union and States must consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Commissions report to the President, who lays the reports before Parliament.

s:
Match List-I (Amendment) with List-II (Effect):
List-I | List-II
a. 77th (1995) | i. Proviso to Article 335 – relaxed qualifying marks
b. 81st (2000) | ii. Consequential seniority w.e.f. 17 June 1995
c. 82nd (2000) | iii. Article 16(4B) – carry-forward of unfilled vacancies
d. 85th (2001) | iv. Article 16(4A) – reservation in promotion
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 77th – 16(4A) promotion quota; 81st – 16(4B) carry-forward; 82nd – proviso to 335 (relaxed marks in promotion); 85th – consequential seniority w.e.f. 17 June 1995.

s:
Match List-I (Case) with List-II (Holding):
List-I | List-II
a. Indra Sawhney (1992) | i. Art. 16(4) only at initial appointment; 50% ceiling
b. E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) | ii. SCs a single class; struck the AP Act 2000
c. M. Nagaraj (2006) | iii. Upheld 77th-85th Amendments; quantifiable data needed
d. Jarnail Singh (2018) | iv. No backwardness data for SC/ST promotion; creamy layer applies
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Indra Sawhney – 16(4) limited to initial appointment, 50% ceiling; Chinnaiah – SCs a single class; Nagaraj – upheld the amendments subject to quantifiable data; Jarnail Singh – no backwardness data needed, creamy layer applies.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In August 2026 the Centre supported an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas.
2. In Punjab v Davinder Singh (2024), a seven-judge Bench by 6:1 allowed sub-classification of SCs and overruled Chinnaiah.
3. Jarnail Singh (2018) applied the creamy layer to SC/ST promotions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Centre opposed an income-based creamy layer, saying any change needs a holistic empirical review.

s:
Match List-I (Incident) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Karamchedu (1985) | i. Sparked the independent Dalit movement in AP
b. Tsundur (1991) | ii. Guntur district, AP
c. Khairlanji (2006) | iii. Supreme Court entrusted monitoring to the Allahabad HC
d. Hathras (2020) | iv. Maharashtra
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Karamchedu (AP, 1985) – sparked the independent Dalit movement; Tsundur (Guntur, AP, 1991); Khairlanji (Maharashtra, 2006); Hathras (UP, 2020) – monitoring by the Allahabad High Court.

s:
Consider the following statements about caste atrocities:
1. The National Commission for SCs and STs (1990) listed land disputes, bonded labour, indebtedness and non-payment of minimum wages as causes.
2. In 2017 the NCRB added a separate head for being forced to leave residence or social boycott.
3. Rajasthan recorded the most crimes against SCs in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Uttar Pradesh topped (57,789 crimes against SCs in all in 2023), followed by Rajasthan and MP.

s:
Match List-I (Movement) with List-II (Date / place):
List-I | List-II
a. Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha | i. 25 December 1927
b. Manusmriti Dahan | ii. 1924-25, Travancore
c. Kalaram Temple Entry | iii. 20 March 1927
d. Vaikom Satyagraha | iv. 1930, Nashik
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Mahad – 20 March 1927 (right to draw water from a public tank); Manusmriti Dahan – 25 Dec 1927; Kalaram Temple Entry – 1930, Nashik (all Ambedkar); Vaikom – 1924-25, Travancore (T.K. Madhavan, Keshava Menon).

s:
Match List-I (Work) with List-II (Author):
List-I | List-II
a. Gabbilam (1941) | i. Gurram Jashuva
b. Gulamgiri (1873) | ii. B.R. Ambedkar
c. Jatimimamsa | iii. Jyotiba Phule
d. Annihilation of Caste (1936) | iv. Sree Narayana Guru
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Gabbilam – Gurram Jashuva (a bat can enter the temple, an untouchable cannot); Gulamgiri – Phule; Jatimimamsa – Sree Narayana Guru; Annihilation of Caste – Ambedkar.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bhagya Reddy Varma praised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as the model for Dalit uplift.
2. Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932 and started the paper Harijan in 1933.
3. Bhagya Reddy Varma founded the Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906), the first Dalit body in Hyderabad State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as paternalistic.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ambedkar declared at Yeola in 1935: 'I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu'.
2. The term 'Harijan' was coined by Ambedkar.
3. Periyar held that political freedom is meaningless without social equality.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Gandhi coined 'Harijan'; Ambedkar stood for legal-constitutional rights and annihilation of caste.
